log: Enemy necromancer used grave bolt for 3 damage.
Enemy wolf used fangs for 3 damage and took 1 in retaliation.
Your adept used spark for 4 damage.
Enemy bone archer used bone bow for 3 damage and took 3 in retaliation.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: The council gave the Overseer his timber and toll charter. With the ledger and the workers’ memories, they can take it away. I will answer for my patrol’s part as well.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The Rootbinder has put his dead on the crossing. He needs the Overseer’s protection and his supply of bodies. He would rather burn this branch than let the families hear it.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Take the bridge fort so the households can cross. Bring Lark to the northern meeting alive; a dead necromancer alone will not open a shared road.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: Dain sent for me. Some of those workers were my neighbors. Stone sparks crack bone; let the shields hold the dead while I clear your road.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The families heard the branch. The council matched the orders to the ledger and revoked the Overseer’s charter.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I have given them my account too. We will harvest the ordinary woods for repairs. Your groves are outside the charter.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: The fort is ours. Village and woodland guards can keep this road together; neither side owns the right to close it.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The Rootbinder still has his dead. But he no longer has a silent village to hide them in.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The first cart crossed today. It carried apples, not axes.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Keep the road open. The roots will do the rest.

campaign.outcome: Mission complete. The company can rest and regroup.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The council promised the villages repair timber. Its Overseer marked our sacred groves instead. His crews keep their tools and carts in those two forts.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Take the camps and the cutting stops. The northern post kept the workers’ records. Bring those back too.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: My missing woodcutters were sent here. The Overseer says your pack killed them. I have orders to protect the crews that remain.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Your orders won’t tell us where they went. Their ledger might.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: We need our roots back, not your bones. Keep away from our groves, captain, and help us find your people.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I suspended my patrol’s orders. These other guards answer to the Overseer. I will stand here with you until we know what happened.

dialogue.speaker: The Overseer
dialogue.text: Dain is dismissed. His truce binds none of you. Destroy the branch and break their circle before the council hears their lies.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: Bring me to the central grove. The roots kept the workers’ last memories. If I am driven out, I must begin again.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then we defend the grove, captain included. The Overseer has given us a reason to keep listening.

dialogue.text: Bring me to the central grove. The roots kept the workers’ last memories. If I am driven out, I must begin again.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Then we defend the grove, captain included. The Overseer has given us a reason to keep listening.

dialogue.speaker: The company
dialogue.text: Lark fell. The company cannot continue without them.

campaign.outcome: Lark fell. The company cannot continue without them.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: I suspended my patrol’s orders. These other guards answer to the Overseer. I will stand here with you until we know what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The workers asked for the pay he owed them and refused to cut this grove. The Overseer handed them to the Rootbinder. He killed them and bound their bodies to the logging crews.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: Unpaid labor for the Overseer. Bodies and protection for the Rootbinder. And my patrol sent to punish you for their murders.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: This branch holds what the roots remember. Their families can hear it too.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: The council is meeting across the river. We take the branch and the ledger there. Let the people who gave him his office judge what he did with it.

campaign.outcome: Mission complete. The company can rest and regroup.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Dain
dialogue.text: The council gave the Overseer his timber and toll charter. With the ledger and the workers’ memories, they can take it away. I will answer for my patrol’s part as well.

dialogue.speaker: Lark
dialogue.text: The Rootbinder has put his dead on the crossing. He needs the Overseer’s protection and his supply of bodies. He would rather burn this branch than let the families hear it.

dialogue.speaker: Alder
dialogue.text: Take the bridge fort so the households can cross. Bring Lark to the northern meeting alive; a dead necromancer alone will not open a shared road.

dialogue.speaker: Tamsin
dialogue.text: Dain sent for me. Some of those workers were my neighbors. Stone sparks crack bone; let the shields hold the dead while I clear your road.
